Question ID: USH_U05_L02_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: SS.912.A.7.3, SS.912.A.7.4

Stimulus: women/status timeline and presidential policy table

Historical ContextEvidence DetailReasoning Task
This lesson connects women's changing status to 1960s presidential policies. You should examine work, education, family roles, feminism, civil rights law, and the policy goals of Kennedy, Johnson, and Nixon-era debates where relevant.Women's roles changed as more women pursued education, paid work, public leadership, and legal equality, while many still faced discrimination and traditional expectations.Explain context and evidence without drifting outside SS.912.A.7.3, SS.912.A.7.4.

Question: Which conclusion is best supported by the evidence detail? (Women and 1960s Presidential Policies)

generalfeedback.text: Use the stimulus, identify the evidence, explain the reasoning, and check the mapped standard before finalizing your answer.

answer.text: Women's roles changed as more women pursued education, paid work, public leadership, and legal equality, while many still faced discrimination and traditional expectations. This evidence matters because it shows this relationship: The President's Commission on the Status of Women and the Equal Pay Act reflected federal attention to workplace inequality.

feedback.text: Correct. This answer uses the stimulus evidence, explains the context and evidence relationship, and stays inside Women and 1960s Presidential Policies and SS.912.A.7.3, SS.912.A.7.4.
